question: Your team uses Claude Code in a TypeScript monorepo. Database migration conventions apply to SQL files under db/migrations/ and to files named *.migration.ts that sit in many packages under packages/. You want these conventions to load automatically, and only when Claude Code edits one of these migration files. Which configuration best meets this goal?

options.text: Package the conventions as a skill in .claude/skills/ that developers invoke before they begin each piece of migration work.
options.reason: A skill is invoked on demand, so it relies on developers remembering to run it. It does not activate conditionally from file paths the way a path-scoped rule does.

options.text: Place the conventions in a CLAUDE.md file inside the db/migrations directory so that a directory-level configuration covers all migration work.
options.reason: A directory-level CLAUDE.md covers only its own directory. It misses the *.migration.ts files that are spread across packages, and the guide prefers glob-pattern rules for conventions that span directories.

options.text: Create one .claude/rules/ file whose YAML frontmatter sets paths: ["db/migrations/**/*.sql", "**/*.migration.ts"] so the rule loads for both kinds of migration file.
options.reason: The paths field of a .claude/rules/ file takes glob patterns, so it can match the SQL files and the scattered *.migration.ts files. The rule then loads only when Claude Code edits a matching file.

options.text: Create one .claude/rules/ file whose YAML frontmatter sets paths: ["db/migrations/**/*", "packages/**/*"] so the rule covers both locations of migration files.
options.reason: The packages/**/* glob matches every file in every package. The rule would then load for non-migration code too, which adds the irrelevant context and token usage that path scoping is meant to avoid.
